name: Kiwi Sizing
summary: Shopify size charts and AI fit recommendations, built to cut returns. From Staytuned.
best_for: apparel and accessory stores where sizing drives returns, and that want charts plus an AI fit recommender without building either: 4.7 stars from 1,216 reviews on 19 September 2026 is a strong base, though the recent ones read differently from the aggregate
skip_if: you sell one-size or non-wearable products, where a size chart answers a question nobody asks, or you need more than ten charts and would land on a tier whose order-volume charges are not published
honest_knock: The free plan is not limited by the chart count most people assume. Three charts is generous for a small catalogue; the real limit is the Kiwi watermark sitting on your storefront, and removing it is what the $7.99 buys. Judge the free tier on whether you can live with that watermark in front of customers, not on how many charts you get. And read the small print above Plus and Ultimate before you upgrade: both add order-volume charges that the App Store listing never quantifies, while Premium says in writing that it has none.

pricing.notes: (read 5 September 2026 and re-read 19 September and 4 November 2026 on apps.shopify.com/kiwi-sizing, no amount changed) Four tiers, and the interesting line is not the price but the sentence under it. Free publishes up to three size charts with 22 templates and unlimited CSV import, and puts a Kiwi watermark on your storefront. Premium is $7.99 a month for up to ten charts, removes the watermark, adds Google Analytics and auto-translation into English and Spanish, and states plainly: no additional monthly charges. Plus, the tier the store marks Popular, is $14.99 for up to twenty charts, ten size recommenders and six languages. Ultimate is $26.99 for unlimited charts and recommenders and 22 languages. Both Plus and Ultimate carry the same caveat that Premium does not: additional charges apply based on order volume, and the listing does not say what those charges are. Import credits are an optional add-on on every paid tier, and all three come with a 14-day free trial. The listing adds that all charges are billed in USD and that recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. So the cheapest paid plan is the only one whose bill you can predict, and the one the store pushes is not.
